text:
sasha: Heads-up — our eval harness is showing a clear quality drop for model-x (quantized) on the QA benchmark after yesterday's infra merge. EM down ~7%. Seen on canary + staging. :eyes:

maria: Ugh. Which commit/PR landed?

sasha: Looks like the tokenizer dependency bump (tokenizer-lib v2.3.0) went in with infra/merge-tokenizer-refactor (commit 7b4f9d). Metrics started drifting right after that run.

kevin: I pulled the runner logs. There's a tokenization mismatch: some answers now split into extra tokens -> alignments shift. Example from runner logs:
```
input: "Who wrote Dune?"
old_tokens: ["Who"," wrote"," Dune","?"]
new_tokens: ["Who"," w","rote"," D","une","?"]
alignment_offset: +2
```

arjun: That explains EM drop (exact match very sensitive). Also saw that batching padding changed ordering in the quantized path — different pad id used in Q8 kernels. Could be two orthogonal changes.

eval-bot: CI alert: eval-ci/job/3421 failed on metric-gate: EM delta -0.071 (threshold -0.02). Full artifact: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/3421/artifacts

maria: Can we repro locally with the older tokenizer pinned vs new? Quick A/B would tell if tokenizer delta alone causes the regression.

sasha: I'm running an A/B now: master@7b4f9d (new tokenizer) vs master^1@3c1a2b (old tokenizer). Using the same seed/inputs. Will post diffs.

kevin: If tokenizer is the culprit, short-term mitigation = pin tokenizer-lib to 2.2.x in the eval-runner image and rerun canary. We should also add a tokenizer-stability test in the harness to catch token-level shifts.

maria: Agree. Also add a gating rule in eval CI to block merges that change token counts distribution beyond small tolerance. We don't have that today.

arjun: For the quant path change I saw, we should add a regression test that compares outputs on float vs quant kernels for small sample seeds. Right now CI only checks end-metrics, so kernel-level divergences slip by.

sasha: A/B done — with old tokenizer EM=0.842, with new tokenizer EM=0.771 on same sample set. So tokenizer accounts for most of the drop (~7%). Quant-pad/ordering accounts for ~1% additional when I toggle the Q8 path.

kevin: Good repro. Plan: 1) revert tokenizer bump in eval-runner image (pin to 2.2.7) and push hotfix canary, 2) add tokenization distribution test and a small token-alignment unit in harness, 3) create a follow-up PR to land tokenizer-refactor with explicit tokenization-compat tests.

maria: I'll own the gating + CI rule. Putting a draft pipeline change here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-ci/pull/178 — it fails fast if token_count_mean delta > 0.02 or token_split_rate > 0.005. Thoughts?

arjun: Looks reasonable. Also suggest logging tokenization fingerprints in the eval artifacts so we can diff quickly next time (mean len, std, top-20 ngrams).

ci-bot: deploy request: eval-runner-hotfix pinned-tokenizer created. Canary deploy started (canary-23). Link: https://deploys.redwood.ai/canary/canary-23

sasha: Thanks — once canary finishes I'll re-run the full harness and report. If green, we rollback the merge from the infra branch or keep it in a separate non-eval image until compatibility tests land.

kevin: I'll open the revert PR now: gh: redwood-inference/infra#512 (revert tokenizer bump). Assigning to me and sasha for quick review.

maria: Assigning CI gating follow-up to me + arjun.

sasha: Owner list: kevin (revert/hotfix), maria (CI gating), arjun (quant kernel test), sasha (re-run + report). If anyone hits blockers ping me. :thumbsup:

maria: quick note — add a tiny eval-case to the dashboard for tokenization drift so ops can watch it in real time (per-route). I'll add a panel.

sasha: Great. Closing loop once canary results are in. Thanks all.
